description: The charge-word definition: words in an issue that name a metered or renewing charge, which admission refuses until the owner decides it. They name charges in the owner's cost definition (docs/contracts/loop-lane/README.md, "Cost, which comes to me"); a subscription login, a lane's subscription credential (its subscription leg, token, fallback or OAuth, and its subscription and fallback legs), Claude subscription usage and a measured pass run on the subscription, model usage that definition calls not cost, match none when the subscription is unqualified or Claude's; a Claude subscription upgrade or purchase and any other vendor's subscription still match, its login and credential words included, when a vendor name (Copilot, GitHub, OpenAI, ChatGPT, OpenRouter, Azure, Microsoft, AWS, Amazon, GCP, Google, Gemini, Cloudflare, Pulumi, Cursor, Bedrock or Vertex) comes before `subscription`, with at most one word between. Intake admission in the marketplace repository (.github/scripts/intake-triage/admit.mjs) reads it for what the issue will do: the title and the body's task items and sections under a `work_headings` heading, or the whole body when it has neither; it reads no comment. Each value is a JavaScript regular expression, matched case-insensitively. `code` is removed from the text first (closed fenced blocks, matched by whole fence lines as CommonMark defines them, and one-line inline code spans, whose opening backtick no backslash escapes), so a job or file name in code is not prose. `cost` refuses on every repository; `cost_private` refuses unless the repository's visibility reads public, since standard GitHub-hosted runner minutes are free there and larger runners are not (https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions). `work_headings` is matched against an ATX heading's text, past any leading markup, and a section runs to the next heading at its level or shallower.
